  Readable gloss: "The gentilic noun Edomi (Hebrew אֲדֹמִי, 'Edomite') designates a person belonging to the nation of Edom, the territory southeast of the Dead Sea settled by the descendants of Esau (Gen 36). The term is applied most memorably to Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman who betrayed the priests of Nob (1 Sam 21:7; 22:9, 18; Ps 52 title). It also appears in reference to Edomite women among Solomon's foreign wives (1 Kgs 11:1) and to the Edomites as enemies in Hadad's narrative (1 Kgs 11:14-17). All twelve occurrences denote the same ethnic identity with only number and gender inflection varying."

Spanish edomita, French Edomite, and German Edomiter confirm one gentilic sense across singular, plural, masculine, and feminine forms.
